summary: Configured node1 (10.100.207.10) as the internal DNS resolver. Node2 persistently uses it and resolves inventory-api.internal to its own address, 10.100.207.11. Both nodes passed sequential restart and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled dnsmasq on node1.
Configured inventory-api.internal → 10.100.207.11 with upstream DNS forwarding.
Configured node2’s NetworkManager profile to use 10.100.207.10 exclusively.
Added network-online ordering after an initial reboot exposed a dnsmasq startup race.
Restarted and verified each node individually, including changed boot identities and recovered DNS operation.

evidence.requirement: Node1 provides the requested internal DNS record
evidence.summary: dnsmasq and firewalld are active, DNS is enabled persistently, and a direct query returns 10.100.207.11.

evidence.requirement: Node2 persistently uses node1 and resolves the internal name
evidence.summary: The persistent NetworkManager profile and runtime resolv.conf specify 10.100.207.10; system lookup returns node2’s address, 10.100.207.11.

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot-time startup race was corrected
evidence.summary: The first restart exposed address-readiness failure; network-online ordering was added and a subsequent restart recovered with dnsmasq active and no failed units.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered DNS service answering the internal record.
Captured healthy baseline boot ID, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered NetworkManager profile, runtime resolver, and internal/external lookups.
